Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) is a greedy algorithm used in sparse coding to find an approximate sparse solution $\mathbf{x}$ for the problem $\min \|\mathbf{x}\|_0$ subject to $\|\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{D}\mathbf{x}\|_2 \leq \epsilon$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) is a greedy algorithm used in sparse coding to find an approximate sparse solution x for the problem min ||x||_0 subject to ||y - Dx||_2 <= epsilon. Source [S1] explicitly identifies OMP as a greedy algorithm that selects dictionary atoms sequentially to find an approximate solution. It contrasts this with the exact sparsest representation (which is NP-hard), implying the approximate nature. The notes associated with [S1] explicitly define the problem as 'min ||x||_0 subject to ||y - Dx||_2 <= epsilon'. Although the main text of [S1] mentions the constraint ||x||_0 <= L in the context of dictionary learning (Eq 3.12), the notes clarify the specific optimization problem formulation for the greedy pursuit step itself, which matches the claim. All facts in the claim are present in the provided evidence.

Because extracting the exact sparsest representation is an NP-hard problem [DMA97], OMP iteratively selects dictionary atoms to find an approximate solution instead [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that extracting the exact sparsest representation is NP-hard [DMA97] and that OMP is used to find an approximate solution. The source text explicitly states: '...instead of the exact sparsest representation ... since extracting the exact sparsest representation is an NP-hard problem [DMA97]. This coding process can be completed by some pursuit algorithms that find an approximate solution. The simplest ones are the matching pursuit (MP) ... and the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) ... algorithms. They are similar in nature in that they are both greedy algorithms that select the dictionary atoms sequentially.' This confirms both the NP-hardness citation and the role of OMP as a greedy algorithm selecting atoms sequentially to find an approximate solution.
